skill.name: algorithmic-art
skill.description: Guides AI assistants to create algorithmic art philosophies and self-contained p5.js HTML viewers with seeded controls.
skill.summary: Create generative art philosophies and p5.js browser artifacts from creative prompts.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: Most static alerts are false positives from Markdown fences, inline file names, CSS, comments, and RegExp.exec used for color parsing. The confirmed issues are low-risk external browser dependencies for p5.js and Google Fonts; no prompt injection attempt or malicious intent was found.

remediation.issue: Generated artifacts load p5.js from a third-party CDN.
remediation.suggestion: Bundle a vetted local copy of p5.js or require pinned SRI and crossorigin attributes in every generated artifact.

remediation.issue: The viewer template imports Google Fonts from external domains.
remediation.suggestion: Use local font files or a system font stack when offline use or privacy-sensitive deployments matter.

remediation.issue: The SKILL.md CDN example omits the SRI protection used by the template.
remediation.suggestion: Update the documentation example to match the template with a pinned version, SRI hash, and crossorigin attribute.

content.value_statement: Generative art can be hard to translate from a vague creative brief. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code to write a philosophy and p5.js viewer.
actual_capabilities: Guides creation of a short algorithmic art philosophy from a user theme.
Defines a workflow for building self-contained p5.js HTML artifacts.
Requires seeded randomness so the same seed can reproduce the same artwork.
Provides a viewer template with sidebar controls, seed navigation, reset, and download actions.
Suggests parameter controls for quantities, scales, probabilities, colors, and thresholds.
Includes a JavaScript reference template for p5.js structure and utility functions.
limitations: Generated HTML still needs manual review before sharing or publishing.
The default viewer depends on external p5.js and Google Fonts URLs.
The skill focuses on browser-based generative art, not image editing or 3D rendering.
Performance depends on the generated algorithm and the viewer device.

use_cases.title: Prototype Generative Art Concepts
use_cases.description: Turn a mood, theme, or reference into a philosophy and an interactive p5.js artwork.

use_cases.title: Explore Visual Directions for Campaigns
use_cases.description: Create seeded visual systems that designers can tune through browser controls.

use_cases.title: Teach Creative Coding Workflows
use_cases.description: Show how concept, parameters, randomness, and interface controls connect in one artifact.

prompt_templates.title: Create a First Artwork
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the algorithmic-art skill to create a calm generative artwork from this theme: [theme]. Include the philosophy and one interactive HTML artifact.

prompt_templates.title: Adapt a Visual Direction
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an algorithmic art piece for [audience] with this mood: [mood]. Make the seed and key visual parameters easy to adjust.

prompt_templates.title: Build Seeded Variations
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a generative system around [concept]. Include a subtle conceptual reference, seeded variation controls, and parameters for density, motion, and color.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Cohesive Series
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the skill to create a gallery-ready generative series from [brief]. Define the philosophy, interaction model, default seed, and three tuned variation seeds.

output_examples.input: A meditation on city rain at night.
output_examples.output: The skill returns a concise philosophy about urban rhythm, then an interactive p5.js viewer with rain-like particles and seed controls.

output_examples.input: A visual system inspired by coral growth and tidal pressure.
output_examples.output: The output describes branching growth rules and provides a browser artifact with sliders for density, flow, curvature, and palette.

output_examples.input: A quiet generative poster for a music festival.
output_examples.output: The skill produces a refined computational concept and an adjustable artwork that can export a PNG from selected seeds.

best_practices: Start with a concise theme, mood, and any required visual constraints.
Review generated HTML before sharing because it runs JavaScript and loads browser dependencies.
Test seed navigation, reset behavior, parameter sliders, and PNG download in a browser.
anti_patterns: Requesting a static image only when the skill is designed for interactive generative systems.
Removing seed controls, which breaks reproducibility and variation exploration.
Treating generated artifacts as production web code without performance and security review.

faq.question: What does this skill create?
faq.answer: It creates an algorithmic art philosophy and a self-contained p5.js HTML viewer with interactive controls.

faq.question: Does it create finished image files directly?
faq.answer: No. It creates browser-based generative art that can include a PNG download action.

faq.question: Can I reproduce the same artwork later?
faq.answer: Yes. The workflow requires seeded randomness so the same seed can reproduce the same result.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use it?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does the default viewer need internet access?
faq.answer: Yes. The template loads p5.js and Google Fonts from external URLs unless the author bundles them locally.

faq.question: Is generated code ready for production?
faq.answer: No. Review the JavaScript, browser dependencies, and performance before publishing or embedding it.
